finalSummary:
Done. All three features are built, wired, and verified against a real boot of the app (`node src/server.js` + curl), plus a 15-check end-to-end pass.

## What I built

**New files:**
- `src/routes/products.js` — the products list endpoint (it didn't exist before) with offset pagination.
- `src/middleware/requestId.js` — assigns/propagates a trace id.
- `src/middleware/requestLogger.js` — one structured log line per request.
- `src/middleware/rateLimit.js` — per-IP fixed-window limiter.

**Changed:** `src/server.js` (wired the middleware in the right order + a JSON error/404 handler), `.env.example` (two new tunables).

## How each ask landed

1. **Pagination** — `GET /products?page=&limit=` returns `{ data, meta }`, where `meta` has `page/limit/total/totalPages/hasNext/hasPrev` so a client can build page controls without guessing. `limit` defaults to 20, caps at 100; junk/negative input falls back to defaults.
2. **Rate limit per IP** — `429` with `Retry-After` once an IP exceeds the window, plus `X-RateLimit-*` headers on every response. Tunable via `RATE_LIMIT_MAX` / `RATE_LIMIT_WINDOW_MS`.
3. **Traceable request id** — every response carries `X-Request-Id` (reused from an upstream header if present, else generated), the same id appears in the log line and in every error body, so a user quoting that header points you straight to the request.

## The one bug worth calling out

My own verification caught it: a negative `limit` (like `-4`) was clamping *up* to 1 instead of falling back to the default. Fixed the parser so anything below the floor is treated as absent → uses the default. This is exactly why I run the checks rather than eyeball the code — the parser *looked* right.
